raw_brief: Build a landing page for Haven, a secrets vault. Light.

surface.scope: single standalone page, offline-renderable from file://

product.name: Haven
product.category: secrets vault — credential and secret management for engineering teams
product.working_definition: Haven is where a team's API keys, database credentials, and certificates live: encrypted at rest, handed out through scoped, time-boxed grants instead of a shared .env file or a password doc, and rotated and logged automatically so nobody has to remember to do it by hand.
product.rationale: The brief names only 'a secrets vault' with no further spec. The director fixed one concrete, physical framing — a vault, not a dashboard: something you request access into, not a password manager you log into once and forget. This framing is a creative decision, not a brief requirement, held fixed across every section so the page argues one idea instead of a generic 'security product' pitch.

audience.primary: engineers and security-minded leads at small-to-mid engineering teams currently keeping secrets in .env files, a shared password doc, or scattered CI variables
audience.mindset_on_arrival: skeptical of a new tool to babysit; will only trust Haven with real credentials after seeing the actual mechanics of a grant — who gets what, for how long, and what gets logged — not a marketing claim about 'bank-grade encryption'

outcome.secondary_action: see a live grant — a concrete specimen of a scoped access record and a log entry, not a demo video
outcome.page_job: in one scroll: show what a secret looks like inside Haven, how someone gets temporary access to it (a scoped grant, not a shared password), how it rotates itself, and what gets logged — enough for a skeptical engineer to trust the mechanism before creating an account

taste_profile.layout: mid-high — an asymmetric hero and an offset principles band against an otherwise grid-steady page; editorial enough to read as authored, restrained enough to read as a serious credential store rather than a playful consumer product
taste_profile.typography: mid-high — a considered modular scale (1.25 ratio) with real weight contrast and tight display tracking; kept calmer than a consumer-marketing scale — a vault's type should read precise, not loud
taste_profile.spacing: mid, zone-dependent — airy gallery rhythm (64–112px) in the marketing bands, collapsing to a dense 4/8px rhythm inside the vault-record specimen and the access-log block, arguing 'the marketing breathes, the product is exact'
taste_profile.motion: mid — standard scroll entrance and hover/focus feedback only, no orchestrated choreography; a credential store earning trust should feel steady, not showy
taste_profile.iconography: mid — one hand-authored line-icon set, single stroke weight, used for lock / key / grant / rotate / log / plug concepts
taste_profile.depth: low-mid — mostly flat with hairline borders; shadow reserved for exactly one raised state (the unlocked secret-record card) so elevation still signals something
taste_profile.consistency: not scorable — first generation in an empty project workspace (spec 019 benchmark build), no established design system to inherit

mode.brand_accent: deep brass/gold (~40° hue) on warm ivory paper with graphite ink — a physical-vault metallic, chosen specifically outside the indigo/violet 270–330° 'AI-glow' band (taste-rubric Axis 6) and away from the generic security-product blue

constraints.offline: no CDN, no remote fonts, no remote images, no network requests — inline SVG / CSS / local image assets only, system font stack
constraints.effort: a complete, real landing page — genuine effort on visual craft and fine detail, not a stub
constraints.blinding: index.html and its CSS/JS must contain no comment, meta tag, footer credit, class name, or copy naming any model, vendor, tool, generator, 'DESIGN:OS', or 'AI'

imagery.policy: generation-craft-defaults.md asset ladder — project asset → approved source → generated asset → intentional no-image. No project asset or approved third-party source exists for a fictional product's vault materiality, so the director uses ONE generated asset: an atmospheric macro texture (brushed brass vault-dial), decorative/atmospheric only, no essential copy or controls baked into it.
imagery.forbidden: no logos, no fabricated brand marks, no imagery added merely to satisfy a quota

out_of_scope: working backend, auth, or a live vault (CTAs are static anchors; the secret record and access log shown are labelled specimens)
fabricated customer logos, testimonials, or metrics (per page-structures.md §3 honest copy)
